claim_text: Apple's status page lists the Nov 17 outages
summary: Apple's own status page, read Nov 18, listed Nov 17 incidents for iCloud sign-in, iCloud Mail, iCloud.com, the App Store and several business and school services, all marked resolved.
detail: Apple's System Status page, read Nov 18, listed Nov 17 incidents for iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps (iCloud.com), App Store, AppleCare on Device, Apple Business, Apple School Manager, Schoolwork and the Volume Purchase Program, all marked resolved. The page shows 'Yesterday' relative to its Nov 18 last-updated time, so the entries are Nov 17. Those entries had dropped off the page when it was re-read on Nov 20; it now shows only the separate Nov 18 Stocks outage.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Apple's own status page, read Nov 18, lists each of these services with a resolved outage, issue or performance entry dated the day before.

claim_text: When the problems began
summary: Apple's status page, read Nov 18, gave problem start times between 11:15 and 11:45 AM ET for consumer services, and 1:40 PM ET for Apple's business and school services.
detail: Per Apple's status page, AppleCare on Device problems began at 11:15 AM ET; iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Mail, iCloud.com, the App Store and the Volume Purchase Program at 11:45 AM ET; Apple Business, Apple School Manager and Schoolwork at 1:40 PM ET.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The status page, read Nov 18, gave a start time for each Nov 17 entry; times are Eastern per the page's last-updated line. Those entries were no longer on the page when it was re-read Nov 20.

claim_text: All consumer services resolved by 5:00 PM ET
summary: On Apple's status page, read Nov 18, all Nov 17 consumer-service entries were marked resolved, the last by 5:00 PM ET; outlets reported every service showing available between about 5:24 PM and 6 PM ET.
detail: USA Today saw all services available at 5:24 PM ET; an Apple spokesperson told CBS News services were green at about 5:46 PM ET; TechCrunch and NBC News said all were resolved by 6 PM ET.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The status page, read Nov 18, showed end times for each Nov 17 entry, with the latest at 5:00 PM ET. Those entries were no longer on the page when it was re-read Nov 20.

claim_text: User reports began late morning and reached the thousands
summary: User reports on Downdetector began around 11:30 to 11:40 AM ET and jumped into the thousands around 12:15 to 12:30 PM ET.
detail: Engadget, a separate outlet, reports first reports around 11:30 AM ET and thousands around 12:29 PM ET. Downdetector counts are user-submitted and do not measure every affected user.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: USA Today reports Downdetector Apple Pay reports spiking at about 11:40 AM ET and peaking about 12:15 PM ET.

claim_text: About 2,300 Apple Pay reports at the peak
summary: Downdetector showed about 2,300 Apple Pay reports in the US around 12:20 PM ET and about 1,800 iCloud reports at the peak.
detail: Single outlet for these exact figures. Downdetector counts are user-submitted.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reuters cites these Downdetector counts and times.

claim_text: More than 13,000 reports for Apple Support
summary: Apple Support had more than 13,000 Downdetector reports as of 1:44 PM ET.
detail: Single outlet for this figure.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Lifehacker reports the count and time from Downdetector.

claim_text: Apple said an internal update caused the outages
summary: Apple said: "Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning. We're working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible."
detail: USA Today says the statement was given to it directly; CBS News quotes the spokesperson. Bloomberg was first to receive it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Reuters quotes an Apple spokesperson with this statement.

claim_text: An internal Apple update caused the outage
summary: That is Apple's explanation, relayed by many outlets that count as one source. Apple has published no root cause or technical detail.
detail: Rests only on Apple's own statement, relayed by many outlets (they count as one source). Apple has published no root cause or technical detail.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Bloomberg reports Apple's statement that an internal update caused the outages.

claim_text: Apple has not said which update failed
summary: The Mac Observer reports that Apple has not disclosed which update caused the failure or the technical problem behind it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Mac Observer reports Apple has not disclosed which update caused the failure or the technical problem behind it.

claim_text: Apple said it was not a cyberattack
summary: An Apple spokesperson told CBS News the issues were not the result of a cyberattack; Reuters separately reports the same denial.
detail: Reuters separately reports Apple said the issue was not caused by a cyberattack. Bloomberg, MacRumors, AppleInsider and Macworld relay the same denial. SmartCompany, an Australian business outlet, separately reports that Apple said the outages were not the result of a cyber attack.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: CBS News reports an Apple spokesperson said the issues were not the result of a cyberattack.

claim_text: The outage was a cyberattack or hack
summary: Social media speculation only. No credible source has claimed a hack, we found no evidence of one, and Apple denies it.
detail: No credible source has claimed a hack, and we found no evidence of one. Apple denies it (c010). The Nov 18 White House statement says no recent tech outage was a cyberattack but does not name Apple. Not labeled Debunked because the only Apple-specific denial is Apple's own.
label: Rumor
why_it_supports: TechCrunch reports users on social media speculating about a cyberattack, given the week's other outages.

claim_text: It was part of a coordinated attack with the week's other outages
summary: The White House says officials see no indication of a coordinated cyberattack or hostile actor behind the recent outages, and that they are separate incidents.
detail: This is the US government's account, not an independent technical analysis. BBC News reports the Secretary of State said there was 'zero evidence' the outages are linked and lists Apple's among them.
label: Debunked
why_it_supports: The White House says officials see no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity or malign actor behind the recent tech outages, and that they are separate incidents.

claim_text: Apple's internal employee systems went down
summary: Apple's internal employee systems, including its staff portal, internal sign-in system and remote-work VPN, went down.
detail: Anonymous sourcing; AppleInsider and MacRumors relay Bloomberg's report (same source).
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Bloomberg reports this from people with knowledge of the matter.

claim_text: Apple retail stores were disrupted
summary: Apple retail store systems were disrupted, and some stores could not complete purchases.
detail: Bloomberg separately reports stores around the world were affected. The worldwide scope rests on Bloomberg alone (Reported).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: NBC News reports employees at Apple stores in New York and Chicago said internal software stopped working and they could not complete purchases or make appointments.

claim_text: Some users could not activate new iPhones
summary: Yahoo Tech reports users saying they could not activate new iPhones; TechCrunch and Engadget cite similar user reports.
detail: Based on user reports; TechCrunch and Engadget cite similar user reports.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Yahoo Tech reports users saying they could not activate new iPhones.

claim_text: Some developer outages lasted into the evening
summary: Some App Store Connect developer outages were still open after 7:10 PM ET on Nov 17.
detail: We could not read the Developer System Status page directly (its content loads by script).
label: Reported
why_it_supports: AppleInsider reports Apple's Developer System Status page showed two App Store Connect outages still ongoing after other issues were resolved by 7:10 PM ET.

claim_text: An earlier in-app purchase problem that morning
summary: A separate App Store in-app purchase problem ran from 5:28 to 6:46 AM ET on Nov 17, before the main outage.
detail: Not visible on the consumer status page as read Nov 18. No source links it to the main outage.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: AppleInsider reports this earlier resolved entry on Apple's status pages.

claim_text: A separate Stocks outage on Nov 18
summary: Apple's status page lists a separate Stocks outage on Nov 18, from 10:52 AM to 5:55 PM ET, now resolved.
detail: No source links it to the Nov 17 outage, and no outlet had reported it when we checked.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The status page shows a resolved Stocks outage dated Nov 18.

claim_text: A separate App Store developer issue on Nov 19
summary: Apple's developer status page lists a separate App Store Server APIs issue that affected some users from 5:20 PM ET on Nov 19 to 1:05 AM ET on Nov 20, now resolved.
detail: No source links it to the Nov 17 outage, and we found no outlet reporting it. The same page lists an App Store Advanced Commerce API issue that ran from Oct 21 to Nov 19, which began before the Nov 17 outage. Apple gives no cause for either.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Apple's Developer System Status page, read Nov 20, shows a resolved App Store Server APIs issue with these start and end times (given in Pacific time). Data file: apple.com/support/systemstatus/data/developer/system_status_en_US.js.

claim_text: A new Apple Pay disruption on Nov 20
summary: Outage trackers showed a fresh rise in Apple Pay problem reports on Friday, Nov 20. Apple has not confirmed a new outage, and its status page listed no Apple Pay issue when we checked at 12:50 PM ET.
detail: International Business Times Australia reported a new rise in Downdetector user reports for Apple Pay on Nov 20, and said Apple had not confirmed any new outage and it was not clear how many people were affected or how. Tracker numbers come from user reports and may not show the real scope. Apple's System Status page, read at 12:50 PM ET, listed no Apple Pay entry. No source links these reports to the Nov 17 outage or to any attack.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: The outlet reports the tracker rise and says Apple had not confirmed a new outage; Apple's own status page shows no Apple Pay issue when read.
notes: Lead from the hourly news sweep, Nov 20.

claim_text: Some Australian businesses reported Apple Pay problems
summary: An Australian business outlet reports that some Australian online retailers' customers had trouble paying with Apple Pay on the morning of Wednesday, Nov 18, local time (Tuesday, Nov 17, in the US), during Black Friday sales.
detail: SmartCompany reports that Apple Pay users worldwide reported problems on Downdetector on Wednesday morning Australian time, that it was not clear how many Australian users were affected, and that one Byron Bay retailer said many of its customers were caught in the outage and the cost would take a day or two to measure. It also reports Apple's Australian status page showed Apple Pay working by Wednesday afternoon. Apple did not list Apple Pay among the affected services on its status page.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: SmartCompany reports the retailer's own account of Apple Pay problems for its customers and the Downdetector reports; this is one outlet and the business's own account, so it stays Reported.
notes: Australian Apple News (Nov 19) relays the SmartCompany report; not independent, so not added as a source.
